messages:
jonathan: Quick follow-up from the attention-kernel RFC — we need to lock down which backend we default to for v1.0: Triton kernels or CUDA/CUTLASS? Short pros/cons and action items please.
maria: TL;DR my vote is Triton for rapid iteration, CUTLASS for peak perf. Triton lets us ship more variants faster.
lee: Agree with maria. Triton gives faster dev turnaround but memory/perf at some points is worse than tuned CUTLASS on A100s.
alice: Important: ops support burden. CUTLASS + custom kernels mean more release engineering and patching. Triton reduces maintenance surface.
dylan: Data point from last week's microbench: for causal-attn (seq=1024, bsz=1) on A100:
```
Triton: 18ms, 12.4GB
CUTLASS: 14ms, 13.8GB
```
Cutlass wins latency but uses more peak GPU mem.
jonathan: Good numbers. How about throughput/latency tail and small-batch cases (bsz 4,8)?
dylan: For batch=4 seq=512:
```
Triton: 22ms avg, lower variance
CUTLASS: 19ms avg, higher 95th
```
Cutlass looks better for throughput but Triton gives steadier tails.
maria: Also consider cross-device portability — Triton works on more perf profiles without per-arch kernel engineering. CUTLASS needs more tuning per compute capability.
alice: Operationally we should prefer a default that minimizes customer-facing regressions. That hints at Triton unless CUTLASS yields >=20% cost/latency win.
sam: Has anyone tested quantized FP8-ish paths? We only have limited CUTLASS FP8 kernels; Triton + fused-quant path is still experimental.
lee: Right — quantization story is uneven. Recommend we keep both: default Triton, fallback/CUTLASS for critical low-latency models or dedicated capacity configs.
jonathan: OK sounds like a hybrid policy. We need concrete rollout plan and gating metrics.
infra-bot: New benchmark job queued: `bench/attn-backend/1853456790` — results ETA 6h.
dylan: Proposed gating metrics (prelim):
- median latency reduction >= 10% on representative suite OR
- cost per token improvement >= 12% AND
- no 95th percentile regression > 5% across prioritized customer traces
If CUTLASS hits those, we auto-enable for Dedicated pools with explicit rollout flag.
maria: +1 to those gates. Add maintainability check: patch/update time estimate <= 3 engineer-days per release cadence or require dedicated SRE support.
lee: Action items:
1) @dylan run full perf matrix (bsz 1/4/8, seq 128/512/1024, FP32/INT8/FP8) across p4a/p100/a100 — due Tue 3/26. (owner: dylan)
2) @alice write ops impact doc: release/rollback story, patch frequency, CI needs — due Fri 3/29. (owner: alice)
3) @maria draft hybrid routing policy: default Triton, CUTLASS opt-in via model config + Dedicated auto-opt if gates pass — due Mon 4/1. (owner: maria)
4) @jonathan add canary plan + rollback playbook for production rollout (include telemetry signals and kill-switch) — due Mon 4/1. (owner: jonathan)
5) @sam coordinate quantization tests and surface missing CUTLASS quant kernels — due Wed 3/27. (owner: sam)
jonathan: Please paste tickets/PRs back here when created.
maria: One more: we should prototype a lightweight perf probe in the runtime that samples both backends for a small % of traffic to collect live delta metrics.
dylan: I'll prototype probe — low overhead, 0.5% traffic, async reporting. If we see consistent wins, we'll flip routing.
alice: Ops note: ensure probe has explicit burn-in and can be turned off via flags. Need metric names and dashboards.
lee: Also add trace-level KV cache effects; CUTLASS's mem footprint changes cache hit dynamics.
jonathan: OK final decision for now: hybrid approach (default Triton, CUTLASS opt-in + auto-enable via gating on Dedicated). Owners/duedates above. We'll reconvene after dylan's perf matrix and infra-bot results.
maria: :thumbsup: thanks all.
infra-bot: bench/attn-backend/1853456790 completed: summary uploaded to /internal/bench-reports/1853456790 (raw CSV + plots).
